Start with the teaching choices below. The [developer reference](#for-developers)
collects all question-block options, supported notation and integration details.
For matrix questions, see [matrix input](matrix-input.qmd); for a basis, a
matrix condition or positive definiteness, see [Python answer tests](python-checker-api.qmd).

## For teachers

### Start with a native export {#start-with-a-native-export}

Install STACK SymPy in your Quarto project and SymPy in the Python environment
that Quarto uses. Add AI Feedback if you want guided hints:

```bash
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy
python -m pip install 'sympy==1.13.3'
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback
```

Add the question filter to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - stack-sympy
```

Export a supported Moodle STACK question as XML and keep it in your project.
Use its filename and exact question name in a Quarto block:

```{.stack-question}
#| file: ../questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| seed: 17
#| variants: 3
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```

This page sits in `docs/`, so its filename starts with `../questions/`. A page
at the project root would use `questions/`. The three variants provide fresh
coefficients; a fixed seed reproduces this port's choices. It does not reproduce
Moodle's random sequence. Omit `feedback: true` if you do not need AI hints.

A learner first presses **Validate answers** to review the interpreted answer,
then **Check answer** to receive a mark. Editing an answer requires validation
again. **Run question tests** appears when `review: true` is selected. Below
each card, **Show source** and **Show STACK source** provide the Quarto block
and question XML for inspection and copying.

### Choose what counts as correct {#what-the-adapter-checks}

| Teaching task | Answer test or feature | Where to start |
|---|---|---|
| Equivalent expressions | `AlgEquiv` | [Rational expressions](../examples.qmd#equivalent-rational-expression); state domain restrictions in the prompt. |
| Expanded, factorized or fractional form | `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac`, `LowestTerms` | [Form-sensitive practice](../index.qmd#try-a-question) and the [form reference](#answer-entry-and-form). `LowestTerms` checks form only; pair it with a value check when value matters. |
| Approximate measurements or written precision | `NumAbsolute`, `NumRelative`, `NumDecPlaces` | [Numerical checks](../examples.qmd#three-numerical-checks). |
| Lists, sets and nested collections | `AlgEquiv`, `Sets`, `SameType`, `EqualComAss` | [Collection examples](../examples.qmd#finite-lists-and-sets); decide whether order and repetitions matter. |
| Boolean expressions and polynomial equations | `AlgEquiv` | [Boolean equivalence](../examples.qmd#boolean-equivalence) and [zero-product equations](../examples.qmd#zero-product-equations). |
| A particular matrix | Matrix input with `AlgEquiv`, `SameType` or `EqualComAss` | [Matrix input and grading](matrix-input.qmd). |
| Any basis of a matrix's null, column or row space | `PythonChecker` with the supplied `basis` function | [Basis questions](python-checker-api.qmd#basis-questions-use-the-matrix-in-the-question). Supply the original matrix and select `nullspace`, `columnspace` or `rowspace` in the JSON `space` option. |
| A matrix with stated properties | `PythonChecker` with the supplied `matrix_property` function or an author-written function | [Matrix conditions](python-checker-api.qmd#matrix-conditions-and-partial-credit), including the [positive-definiteness walkthrough](python-checker-api.qmd#author-the-spd-checker). |
| Another mathematical rule | `PythonChecker` | [Custom checker API](python-checker-api.qmd#for-developers). |
| Partial credit and targeted feedback | Weighted response trees (PRTs) | [Three numerical checks](../examples.qmd#three-numerical-checks) and [determinant-one conditions](../examples.qmd#find-a-nonidentity-matrix-with-determinant-one). |
| Guided hints | Optional AI Feedback | [Choose a teaching policy](#choose-a-teaching-policy). |

The [question corpus](../corpus.qmd) shows unchanged imports and the features
that still need adaptation. The [detailed semantics for STACK authors](../compliance/semantics.html#author-attention)
explain important differences from Moodle. This is a defined subset of STACK;
unsupported authoring features stop the build instead of receiving an invented
grading rule.

### Choose a teaching policy {#choose-a-teaching-policy}

AI Feedback gives guided questions, concepts, procedures and a worked solution.
It supports **copy-prompt mode** and a learner-configured provider. Deterministic
answer tests still award the marks; AI Feedback does not grade the response.

Choose the material that should accompany a request for help:

| Context option | What the feedback sees |
|---|---|
| `context: auto` | Visible teaching prose in the preceding section; this is the default. |
| `context: expansion-hint` | The teaching block tagged with that ID. Use comma-separated IDs for several blocks. |
| `context: none` | The question and current response, without nearby teaching prose. |

For example, tag a short explanation with `.ai-context` and reference it from
the question:

````markdown
::: {#expansion-hint .ai-context}
Distributivity gives $a(b+c)=ab+ac$.
:::

```{.stack-question}
#| file: questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| feedback: true
#| context: expansion-hint
```
````

`feedback-language` chooses the explanation language; otherwise the document's
language is used. A named `feedback-policy` can change the sequence or word
limit. The [rational-expression example](../examples.qmd#equivalent-rational-expression)
uses a guiding question followed by a worked explanation. The
[policy configuration reference](#policy-configuration) explains how to define
and select these policies.

Feedback uses the current answer, visible question and selected context. A
matching answer check may supply its status and score. Teacher answers, source
panels, question tests, Python code and detailed grader messages are excluded.
Provider keys are not embedded in the page. Editing removes stale feedback and
check evidence; choosing another variant restarts the hints.

### Validate and publish {#validate-and-publish}

Keep tests for alternate correct answers, common mistakes and the intended
partial credit. Run the question's author tests, render the page, and review
its variants before publishing:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=_extensions/stack-sympy python -m stack_sympy.cli test \
  --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
quarto render
python -m http.server --directory _site 8000
```

Serve the page over HTTP, including locally. Opening an HTML file directly is
not a reliable way to run browser workers. The first answer check downloads
Pyodide and SymPy, so learners need network access. Grading then runs in the
browser. The page does not provide Moodle's attempt history or persistence.

While adapting a question, `diagnostics: true` displays a build problem in the
page. Remove that option before publication so an unsupported question stops
the build. Compare representative responses in Moodle when native STACK
compatibility matters for your assessment.

### Questions with many correct answers {#extend-the-python-port}

An input model is one valid response, not a list of everything a learner may
submit. Select the supplied `basis` or `matrix_property` function with a
choice in its JSON options object, or register your own function for another
condition.
The normal response-tree
branches still decide the credit. The [Python answer-test guide](python-checker-api.qmd)
contains the teacher workflow and a complete developer walkthrough for
positive definiteness.

## For developers

### Question-block options {#question-block-options}

All options below are written as `#| key: value` inside a `.stack-question`
block. File paths are relative to the containing `.qmd` page.

| Option | Default or requirement | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | Required | XML filename. |
| `question` | Required | Exact XML question name. |
| `seed` | `1`; signed 32-bit integer | Starting seed for repeatable variants. |
| `variants` | `1`; from 1 to 20 | Number of variants prepared at build time. |
| `review` | `false` | Show **Run question tests** for the selected variant. |
| `diagnostics` | `false` | Display build errors while authoring. |
| `feedback` | `false` | Enable the separately installed AI Feedback extension. |
| `context` | `auto` | Nearby prose, `none`, or comma-separated context IDs. |
| `feedback-language` | Document `lang` | Language for AI explanations. |
| `feedback-policy` | Inherited policy | Name of a policy loaded by the shared feedback extension. |
| `label` | Generated card ID | Stable exercise key for policy overrides. A Quarto block ID also identifies a card. |
| `python-checkers` | Omitted | Python filename read during the build; register named functions in `CHECKERS`. No source manifest is required. |

The base extension requires Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.13.3, Quarto 1.4+ and HTML
output with JavaScript. AI Feedback requires version 0.8.0+ of that extension
and Quarto 1.8.27+. Set `STACK_SYMPY_PYTHON` to the Python interpreter to use
when Quarto's default interpreter is not the required environment.

### Input and XML reference {#input-and-xml-reference}

The source is a Moodle STACK `<quiz>` containing named `<question type="stack">`
entries. Category and description entries are skipped. Retain inputs, PRTs,
deployed seeds and `<qtest>` cases. Unsupported fields and HTML/CASText fail
with a question-specific location.

| XML input setting | Handling |
|---|---|
| `type` | `algebraic`, scalar `numerical`, or rectangular `matrix`. |
| `tans` | The input's model answer. A PRT node's `tans` is a separate test argument. |
| `strictsyntax`, `insertstars` | Strict syntax is required. Insertion mode `0` requires explicit `*`; mode `1` also accepts adjacent products. |
| `forbidwords`, `forbidfloat` | Reject configured words or decimal literals. |
| `requirelowestterms` | Reject reducible written integer fractions during validation. |
| `checkanswertype` | Check the supported STACK applicability/type rule; this is not a full shape or equality check. |
| `mustverify`, `showvalidation` | Verification metadata and preview visibility are retained; this UI always requires validation before grading. Supported visibility values are `0`, `1`, `3`. |
| `syntaxhint`, `boxsize` | Parse the authored hint and size text fields within the supported limits. |
| `matrix` | Optional fixed/resizable dimension settings; see [matrix input](matrix-input.qmd#for-developers). |

`allowwords` and input `options` must be empty; nondefault syntax attributes
and other insertion modes are unsupported. Question-level `assumereal` and
`assumepositive` affect symbolic assumptions. `questionsimplify=0` preserves
supported written forms when they survive variant preparation; unsupported
held expressions fail clearly.

CASText supports `{@expression@}` for scalars, collections and matrices, and
`{@left=right@}` for a displayed scalar equality. The placeholders
`[[input:name]]`, `[[validation:name]]` and `[[feedback:name]]` connect the
question text to inputs and response trees. HTML is sanitized. This does not
provide arbitrary Maxima evaluation or all STACK text directives.

### Answer entry and form {#answer-entry-and-form}

Supported scalar notation includes arithmetic `+ - * / ^` (also `**`),
parentheses, symbols and the constants `%pi`, `%e`, `%i`. Functions are `sqrt`,
`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `sec`, `csc`, `cot`, `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `sech`, `csch`,
`coth`, `exp`, `log`, `abs`, rational-polynomial `gcd` and real scalar `mod`.
Aliases are `ln`, `cosec`, `cosech`. `mod(x,0)=x` follows Maxima's convention.
With insertion mode `1`, `2x`, `2(x+1)` and `(x+1)(x-1)` are products; `xy`
remains one symbol and spaces alone never imply multiplication.

Form tests `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac`, `LowestTerms` require a direct
input name in `sans`. `EqualComAss` preserves structure up to commutative and
associative reordering. `FacForm` requires one polynomial variable in
`testoptions` and handles univariate rational polynomials. `SingleFrac` checks
an equivalent single written fraction or atomic answer. `LowestTerms` checks
written integer fractions and supported denominator restrictions, without
comparing the teacher value or cancelling symbolic polynomial factors.

`NumAbsolute` and `NumRelative` use the configured tolerance; omitted or
syntactically malformed options default to `0.05`. `NumDecPlaces` requires an
explicit count from 1 to 50 and checks trailing zeros as written precision.
Use a numerical answer test for an approximate measurement rather than treating
algebraic equivalence as a tolerance test.

### Lists, sets and equations {#lists-sets-and-equations}

Lists use `[...]`; sets use `{...}`. Both may nest and be empty. Limits are 32
entries per container, six collection levels and 128 total collection nodes,
with scalar expression leaves. List comparison is ordered. Set comparison
normalizes members without a general proof of every possible scalar identity;
see [set conventions](../compliance/semantics.html#finite-sets).
`Sets` explains outer duplicates and missing/extra members. `EqualComAss`
retains list order, nested boundaries and repeated set entries. `SameType`
follows applicability: two sets have the same type, and different-length lists
can have the same type. It does not establish equality.

Use exact fractions in sets and prepared author collections. Direct decimal
list entries have narrower support: literal constant arithmetic with integer
powers works; decimal-bearing functions, symbolic terms, transformed collections
and transitive author aliases do not. Collection tests require a direct learner
input, preserving the literal arithmetic used by the comparison.

`AlgEquiv` also supports Boolean constants and `and`, `or`, `not`, `implies`,
`xor`, `xnor`, with `nounand`, `nounor`, `nounnot` aliases and at most eight
Boolean variables. Supported polynomial equations and their disjunctions use
a product-of-residuals rule: `a=0 or b=0` matches `a*b=0`. Root multiplicity is
retained. Conjunctions/negations of equations, variable denominators and mixtures
of equations with Boolean propositions are unsupported. Principal complex
roots and logarithms require attention to their domains; the
[conventions reference](../compliance/semantics.html) records the
known differences and proof limits.

### Author variables and helpers {#author-variables-and-helpers}

Exact arithmetic has a 16,384-bit computation budget for rational numerators
and denominators, including intermediate values. Conservative size estimates
reject oversized powers before constructing their integers, including arithmetic
held for equation and written-form checks. This applies to scalar answers and matrix
cells; a custom checker may impose a smaller domain, such as 256-bit rationals.

Write assignments as `name:expression;`; list indexing is 1-based. In addition
to the scalar functions above, authors can use:

| Purpose | Supported helpers |
|---|---|
| Variants | `rand`, `rand_with_step`. |
| Scalar algebra/calculus | `diff`, `expand`, `factor`, `ratsimp`, `cancel`, `ev(expr)`, `ev(expr,simp)`, `num`, `denom`, integer `lcm`. |
| Decimal/significant-figure display | `decimalplaces`, `dispdp`, `displaydp`, `significantfigures`, `dispsf`. |
| Finite collections | `set`, `setify`, `listify`, `union`, `intersection`, `setdifference`, `member`, `subsetp`, `cardinality`. |
| Model basis generation | `nullspace_basis`, `columnspace_basis`, `rowspace_basis`. The basis checker still receives the original matrix. |

`ratsimp` preserves a supported common-denominator form. `listify(list)` keeps
order; sorting a set with `listify` supports rational scalar members only.
Finite helpers require normal simplification and exact fractions. Prepare their
results in question variables before using form-sensitive collection tests;
helper feedback variables and held helper execution are unsupported. `float`
is recognized, but floating-point author values cannot be stored in prepared
variants and are rejected. Learners cannot call author-only helpers.

### Policy configuration {#policy-configuration}

Loading definitions with `policy-files` or `page-policy-files` does not select
a policy. Select `project-policy` or `page-policy` explicitly; STACK uses the
shared `math-exercise` policy namespace. This site's configuration is:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
```

A named policy can inherit settings and replace its hint sequence:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
```

Place this definition in a policy YAML file and select
`feedback-policy: two-step-practice` on a card. A stable `label` targets
`exercises.math-exercise` overrides. The policy resolver applies defaults,
project/page selections, exercise overrides, the selected policy and its
ancestry, then the current step. `steps` replaces the inherited list;
`base-prompt` supplies ongoing instructions and `step-prompt` one step.
The retired `prompt`, inline `integrations` and inline `defaults` settings
are rejected. See the [shared policy reference](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback/blob/main/docs/feedback-policies.md).

Edits cancel stale responses and clear grading evidence while retaining hint
progress. Check resets hints by default; `reset-on-run: false` preserves progress.
Changing variants always resets hints. Only a displayed reply or a generated
copy prompt advances the step. `.ai-feedback-context` and `.math-exercise-context`
are aliases of `.ai-context`. Explicit `jsxgraph:diagram-id` references can include
visual context through the shared extension; diagrams are not collected implicitly.

### Tests, runtime and contribution {#tests-and-evidence}

PRTs are acyclic response-tree graphs with `=`, `+`, `-` branch score operations,
feedback, notes and weighted aggregation. Branch-specific penalties are not
supported. Native `<qtest>` cases check scores, initial-attempt penalty and
ordered answer notes, including anchored notes and `NULL`. The browser has no
Moodle attempt state. For custom predicates, also select the checker filename
on CLI tests; see the [Python guide](python-checker-api.qmd#for-developers).

The same Python core runs locally and in a Pyodide worker. Quarto prepares
variants at build time; the worker validates, grades and replays tests. A worker
timeout can stop runaway grading. The [native comparison](../compliance/) and
[project regression report](../compliance/port-regressions.html) provide separate
evidence, not a blanket compatibility claim. These reports are generated by CI;
a normal `quarto render` does not rerun their mathematical comparisons.

For a source checkout, install `requirements-dev.txt`, run
`PYTHONPATH=_extensions/stack-sympy python -m pytest -q tests`, check the runtime
bundle with `python scripts/bundle_runtime.py --check`, and consult the
[development guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#design-and-contribution)
for browser/native checks. Include a minimal XML question and its qtests when
reporting a grading issue. General matrix arithmetic, inequalities, units,
arbitrary Maxima scripts and Moodle's full attempt workflow remain unsupported.
